summary: With every outstanding receipt already interpreted, the next judgment-changing step was to test whether the finding is RawNode-specific: applications deliver peer messages through the public Node interface, which wraps the same filter. Registered child question @inbound_forget_node_api and requested one new fixed experiment — a fifth test function that drives a real Node started by RestartNode (goroutine, channels, Ready/Advance loop) through a real leader's real heartbeat via Node.Step, a local-type control from a peer, the peer-form MsgForgetLeader, and finally Node.ForgetLeader on the same node. Observations come only from Node.Status and the returned errors, and the harness polls the node's own reported status with a bounded ceiling instead of assuming wall-clock timing (it runs natively with the predicted observations: lead 1 after the heartbeat, unchanged by the local type, 0 after the forged message, and 1 -> 0 through the intended local API). Validation passed with the execution requested; the receipt and its interpretation are pending.
